`tags.indexOf("draft") !== -1` asks for a position and then throws it away. `tags.includes("draft")` asks the question you mean, and there is no `-1`, `0`, `>` or `>=` to get wrong.

The rule reports `!== -1`, `!= -1`, `> -1`, `>= 0`, `=== -1`, `== -1` and `< 0` after a call of `indexOf()`. It does not know types, so any object with an `indexOf` method is reported.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
if (tags.indexOf("draft") !== -1) {
  hide(post);
}

if (email.indexOf("@") < 0) {
  reject(email);
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
if (tags.includes("draft")) {
  hide(post);
}

if (!email.includes("@")) {
  reject(email);
}
```

Code that uses the position is fine:

{/* good */}
```js
const at = email.indexOf("@");
const hasName = email.indexOf("@") > 0;
```
